subject: ventures/fitness-studio-membership-calculator
professional: a boutique-fitness studio owner/operator or fitness-business consultant who runs membership economics for yoga, pilates, cycling and CrossFit studios; they check first that churn is cancellations over start-of-month members and that lifetime value is contribution (not revenue) over churn, then whether CAC counts only paid joins, whether a growth scenario charges for the joins it adds, whether a price rise is assumed to cost no members, and whether class capacity caps the member count

evidence.correctness: Independent Python model (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/445518b1-5429-5297-9052-042574ff3b55/scratchpad/fit/model.py) written from studio-finance practice, not from calc.mjs: expected tenure by summing a cohort survival curve (sum of (1-c)^k, 100,000 terms) instead of 1/c, stock-flow closed form m_t = S + (m0 - S)(1-c)^t instead of the loop, contribution = P(1 - card%) - card fixed - variable, blended CAC, break-even = ceil((fixed + marketing)/contribution), capacity = classes x 52/12 x spots. Compared with `node run.mjs` on the shipped defaults: contribution 140.379, tenure 16.667 months, LTV $2,339.65, CAC $128.57, payback 0.916 months, LTV/CAC 18.20, break-even 138 members, 2,912 spots, 55.6% utilization, full at 323 members, steady state 233.33, month-12 members 207.95 and profit $9,891.94, 12-month cumulative $99,989.56, all four scenario deltas (+2,528.66 / -2,291.38 / +2,019.20 / +6,130.82): every figure equal to the cent. Not 4: with adSpend 0 the page prints 'lifetime value is Infinityx that cost' (cac = 0, index.html:129 divides unguarded), and at churn below 1.1% the '1 point less churn' scenario is clamped to 0.1% (churn 0.5 runs 0.4 points less, still labelled one point).
evidence.completeness: README features exercised in node and by the shipped tests: contribution, LTV, CAC, payback, steady state, month-by-month projection, break-even members, capacity and utilization with member capacity, four scenarios, five warnings, CSV export (toCsv, 13 rows for 12 months), usage counter with opt-out. All work; no TODOs or stubs. The served page https://marisstella.app/fitness-studio-membership-calculator/ returns 200 and serves calc.mjs (200); the served llms.txt carries the marisstella.app URL. Gaps: the Infinity ratio string when marketing is 0; 0 classes a week with typed visits reports 0.0% utilization and 'full at about 0 members' with no warning.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject dir: 23 tests, 23 pass, 0 fail (104 ms). Seven hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with `git checkout -- calc.mjs`: 2 caught, 5 survived. Caught: break-even Math.ceil -> Math.round (1 fail); lifetime 100/churn -> 100/churn - 1 (1 fail). Survived: 'Price up $10' scenario actually +$1 (the test only checks change > 0); profitNow drops marketing spend (no test reads profitNow or the 'does not cover fixed costs' warning); utilization warning threshold 0.85 -> 0.95; LTV/CAC warning threshold 3 -> 2; above-steady-state warning 1.05 -> 1.5. The headline-number tests (LTV, CAC, projection, capacity) are sound; the scenario magnitudes, today's profit, settled profit and every warning threshold are unpinned.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (105 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html module script (lines 113-151), usage.mjs imports. Pure dependency-free core, validation names each bad field, output escaped where strings are user-derived (scenario labels, warnings). Defects: ltv/cac computed in the page template with no guard (index.html:129) so cac = 0 shows 'Infinityx'; the scenario churn clamp (calc.mjs:86) silently changes what the row means while keeping the label; zero classes with visits passes silently (calc.mjs:75-78); the result HTML is built in 400-character one-line string concatenations (index.html:129-131), hard to review.
evidence.claims: Checked: page FAQ 'At 6% churn the average member stays about 17 months' (16.67, pass); 'LTV is contribution, not revenue, and is not discounted' (calc.mjs:66-68, pass); 'count settles ... joins divided by churn' (calc.mjs:71, pass); 'placeholder data, not benchmarks' stated (index.html:58); disclaimer, no-SLA and privacy footer present on page and README; privacy backed (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/sendBeacon; usage.mjs is local storage). Unbacked: README:7 'decide whether to spend the next dollar on ads or on retention' -- neither lever has a cost in the tool: the '5 more new members a month' scenario adds joins with marketing spend unchanged (calc.mjs:89, project() keeps adSpend), and '1 point less churn' costs nothing, so the table compares two free changes and cannot answer a spend decision. 'What ten dollars more on price is worth' (index.html:57) assumes no member leaves over the rise; the README 'Not modelled' list does not name price elasticity. Source llms.txt points at duncan-haywood.github.io; the served one is rewritten to marisstella.app (source-only, not filed). The served breadcrumb files the tool under 'Restaurant, bar & food truck pricing'.
evidence.fitness: Walked an owner's job: 180 members at $149, 6% churn, 14 joins, $1,800 ads, $17,500 fixed. The tool gives LTV, CAC payback, break-even 138, settling at 233, and what churn is worth -- a useful first look an owner can check by hand. Gaps a studio owner hits in the first hour: one price only (no unlimited vs 8-class vs class-pack tiers, no intro-offer-to-member conversion, which is how boutique studios actually acquire); CAC is spend over all joins, so referrals and walk-ins dilute it; the growth scenario adds joins for free; lifetime is uncapped (churn 0.1% gives 1,000 months and an LTV of $140,379); capacity is computed but never caps the projection or the steady state; churn is one flat rate though early-tenure churn dominates in studios.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard subscription/studio unit economics (LTV = margin per member-month / monthly churn; CAC payback = CAC / margin; steady state = joins / churn; capacity = classes x 4.33 x spots). The core formulas are standard and right (recomputed above). Departures a consultant would flag: (1) the +5 joins scenario charges no acquisition cost (at the tool's own CAC that is about $643/month, a third of the $6,131 gain, before any rise in marginal CAC); (2) price rise with zero churn response; (3) blended rather than paid CAC; (4) no lifetime cap or discounting (consultants commonly cap at 24-36 months for studios); (5) projected members can exceed class capacity with no constraint (capacity 323 members at 9 visits; joins 30 at 6% churn settle at 500 with only the 85% warning on today's members, not projected ones).

verdict: A small, clean membership-economics calculator whose numbers are right: an independent cohort-survival and closed-form stock-flow model reproduced LTV, CAC, payback, break-even, capacity, the 12-month projection and all four scenario deltas to the cent. It falls short of the bar on claims and verification: the README sells it as the way to decide between ads and retention, but neither scenario carries a cost and the +5 joins row adds members for free, and 5 of 7 seeded mutations (scenario magnitude, today's profit, every warning threshold) leave the 23 tests green. A studio consultant would use it for a first look at LTV and churn value, then hit single-price, blended-CAC, uncapped-lifetime and no-capacity-constraint limits within the hour. Does not meet the bar (verification 2, claims 2, median 2); finished on what it lists.
